standard.title: Diversity of First Nations visual arts
standard.description: investigate the diversity of First Nations Australians' artworks and arts practices, considering culturally responsive approaches to Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have some awareness that First Nations Australians have rich artistic traditions. They have not yet investigated the diversity of these practices in depth, nor engaged systematically with ICIP rights frameworks.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate the diversity of First Nations Australians' artworks and arts practices with genuine cultural responsiveness, understanding and applying ICIP rights frameworks.

nodes.label: Understanding ICIP rights and protocols
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain what ICIP rights are, why they exist, and what culturally responsive engagement with First Nations artworks looks like in practice
nodes.minimum_width: Explain what ICIP rights are and give one example of what respectful engagement with First Nations cultural material looks like in a visual arts context
nodes.typical_width: Investigate ICIP rights frameworks and explain how they apply to different scenarios — using cultural material in own work, selecting source material for collage, referencing traditional imagery
wider: Investigate a specific case of cultural appropriation in visual arts — explain what ICIP rights were denied, who was harmed, and what a respectful alternative would have looked like
Research how professional artists and design companies obtain permission to use cultural material belonging to a collective rather than an individual
Develop own practical guidelines for engaging with First Nations cultural material in visual arts practice — ground them in specific protocol sources endorsed by First Nations organisations

response_modes.reason: Students commonly understand ICIP rights in the abstract without being able to reason through specific scenarios — they know 'you need permission' without being able to work out who to ask, what counts as cultural material, or what respectful engagement looks like in practice. Scaffolding the scenario-based reasoning (who created this, whose story is it, what permission is needed, how do I obtain it?) builds actionable understanding rather than declarative awareness.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The cultural appropriation case study direction is genuinely rich — it requires students to reason about harm, rights and alternatives in a concrete case, connecting ICIP principles to real consequences. Advancing students who investigate specific professional practice (how design companies obtain collective permission) gain practical understanding that goes well beyond awareness.
success_criteria: Explains what ICIP rights are and why they exist
Gives at least one specific example of what respectful engagement looks like in practice
Does not reduce ICIP to a checklist — explains the reasoning behind the protocols

nodes.label: Investigating diversity of First Nations visual arts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate the diversity of First Nations Australian artworks and arts practices — across regions, styles, media and contexts — with cultural responsiveness
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate at least one First Nations Australian artwork or arts practice in depth; explain what makes it distinctive and culturally significant
nodes.typical_width: Investigate First Nations Australian artworks and practices from at least two different regional or cultural contexts; analyse what is distinctive about each and what connects them; approach the investigation with genuine cultural responsiveness
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australian artists work across multiple artforms — analyse how visual elements interact with performance, music or storytelling to produce layered cultural meaning

Investigate contemporary First Nations Australian artists who are engaging with digital media or international art contexts — analyse how they navigate cultural identity and ICIP responsibilities in these spaces
Research how First Nations Australian visual arts practices have changed and adapted over time while maintaining cultural continuity

response_modes.reason: Students commonly treat First Nations Australian visual arts as a monolithic tradition rather than understanding the enormous diversity across hundreds of distinct cultural groups, regions, media and contexts. Investigating multiple distinct practices — from different regions, media, and contemporary/traditional contexts — resolves this misconception through genuine breadth rather than a single example.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The contemporary First Nations artists in digital and international contexts direction is rich — it challenges students to think about how artists navigate identity, cultural protocol and ICIP responsibilities in contemporary global art spaces. This is genuinely complex territory that goes well beyond the minimum investigation task.
success_criteria: Investigates at least one First Nations Australian artwork or practice in genuine depth
Explains what makes it culturally significant — not just describes what it looks like
Demonstrates cultural responsiveness throughout — not just awareness of protocols

nodes.label: Applying culturally responsive approaches in visual arts
nodes.checkpoint: Students can make ethical choices about how they engage with First Nations Australian visual arts, applying ICIP protocols to their own practice as viewers, researchers and makers.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least one ICIP protocol question to own practice; explain the reasoning behind the protocol.
nodes.typical_width: Apply multiple protocol questions to own practice as a viewer, researcher and maker; explain how the protocols guide ethical engagement with First Nations Australian visual arts.
wider: Evaluate a scenario in which a creator used First Nations Australian visual arts without following ICIP protocols — analyse the ethical issues and what should have been done differently.
Develop a set of personal guidelines for culturally responsive engagement with First Nations Australian visual arts, grounded in specific protocols.
success_criteria: Applies at least one ICIP protocol question to a real or hypothetical visual arts practice scenario
Explains the ethical reasoning behind the protocol

response_modes.reason: Applying protocols requires reasoning through specific situations — the ethical logic does not transfer automatically from principle to practice.
